questions.text: Ayla wishes to estimate the number of trees on a square block of land measuring $1000$ m by $1000$ m. She counts the number of trees on a $5$ m by $5$ m section of the block and finds there are $8$ trees. Based on this, estimate the number of trees on the entire square block of land.

questions.text: In a tropical drink, the ratio of pineapple juice to mango juice to orange juice is $15 : 9 : 4$. (a) How much orange juice is needed if the tropical drink is to contain $3$ litres of pineapple juice? (b) The internal dimensions of a drink container, in the shape of a rectangular prism, are shown. Diagram: $40$ cm by $35$ cm by $20$ cm, NOT TO SCALE. To completely fill the container with the tropical drink, how many litres of mango juice are required?

questions.current_path: Year 12 – Standard 2 / Algebraic relationships / Simultaneous linear equations
questions.text: There are two tanks on a property, Tank A and Tank B. Initially, Tank A holds $1000$ litres of water and Tank B is empty. (a) Tank A begins to lose water at a constant rate of $20$ litres per minute. The volume of water in Tank A is modelled by $V = 1000 - 20t$ where $V$ is the volume in litres and $t$ is the time in minutes from when the tank begins to lose water. On the grid below, draw the graph of this model and label it as Tank A. Grid: $V$ 0 to 1000 against $t$ 0 to 50. (b) Tank B remains empty until $t = 15$ when water is added to it at a constant rate of $30$ litres per minute. By drawing a line on the grid on the previous page, or otherwise, find the value of $t$ when the two tanks contain the same volume of water. (c) Using the graphs drawn, or otherwise, find the value of $t$ (where $t > 0$) when the total volume of water in the two tanks is $1000$ litres.

questions.text:
A salesperson is interested in the relationship between the number of bottles of lemonade sold per day and the number of hours of sunshine in the day. The diagram shows the dataset used in the investigation and the least-squares regression line. Points plotted are (2, 8), (3, 11), (5, 19), (6, 22), (9, 30) on axes Number of hours of sunshine (x) from 0 to 10 and Number of bottles sold (y) from 0 to 32. A dashed regression line passes through about (0, 2) and (9, 31).
(a) Find the equation of the least-squares regression line relating to the dataset.
(b) Suppose a sixth data point was collected on a day which had 10 hours of sunshine. On that day 45 bottles of lemonade were sold. What would happen to the gradient found in part (a)?

questions.text:
For a sample of 17 inland towns, height above sea level ($x$ metres) and average maximum daily temperature ($y$ degrees Celsius) were recorded. Regression line $y = 29.2 - 0.011x$, correlation $r = -0.494$.
For the same towns, latitude ($x$ degrees south) and average maximum daily temperature ($y$ degrees Celsius) are shown. Regression line $y = 45.6 - 0.683x$, correlation $r = -0.897$. Another town is 540 m above sea level and at 28 degrees south.
(a) (i) Use the height equation to predict temperature for a town 540 m above sea level (1 dp). (a) (ii) Interpret the gradient -0.011. (b) Which of height or latitude is better to predict temperature? Give a reason.
